Power curve over a grid of sample sizes

Source: R/curve.R
ape_curve.Rd

Runs the power simulation at each element of n and collects the results. Works for APE and AIE designs alike.

Usage

ape_curve(
  dgp,
  n,
  claim = c("minimum", "detect", "equivalence"),
  sesoi = NULL,
  conf = 0.95,
  nsim = 1000,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'powerape_curve'
plot(x, target_power = NULL, ...)

Arguments

dgp

A powerape_dgp after set_ape() or set_aie().

n

Integer vector (length >= 2) of total sample sizes.

claim

"minimum" (default), "detect", or "equivalence".

sesoi

Smallest effect size of interest, in APE units. Required for "minimum" and "equivalence"; optional for "detect" (if supplied, the outcome table is still broken out against it).

conf

CI level (default 0.95).

nsim

Replications per grid point.

seed

Optional; grid point i uses seed + i - 1.

x

A powerape_curve object.

target_power

Optional horizontal reference line; when the curve crosses it, the crossing n is marked and annotated.

...

Passed to the base plot call.

Value

A powerape_curve object with a results data frame (n, power, mcse, failed).

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- ape_dgp(focal = pa_var("treat", "binary", p = 0.5), baseline = 0.30)
d <- set_ape(d, target = 0.10)
cv <- ape_curve(d, n = c(300, 600, 900), claim = "detect", nsim = 300, seed = 1)
plot(cv, target_power = 0.8)

# }
